newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee falls, forex deposit freeze denied.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee falls, forex deposit freeze denied.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday denied rumours that the government would freeze foreign exchange deposit accounts of residents and non-residents.
"The State Bank would like to categorically state that it is legally not possible to freeze or deny the encashment of foreign currency deposits of residents and non-residents," an SBP statement said.
Before the denial, the Pakistani rupee plunged 0.65 to 41 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday, a dealer said. The dollar was not available in the open market.
A senior official of a foreign bank said private dealers were spreading the rumours, which were not true. "Dealers hammered the rupee in order to make windfall profits."
"The public is urged to pay no attention to this type of rumours which are meant only to create scare and nervousness in the market with the objective of making speculative gains," the SBP said.

An executive of a Pakistani bank said some $100 million were withdrawn from foreign exchange deposit accounts on Sunday and Monday and one Pakistani bank was preparing to pay $150 million to foreign depositors on Tuesday.
The SBP rate, last changed on September 10, was 36.9700/37.1549 rupees to the dollar.
